newsitem.title: USA: U.S.-Cuba migration talks set for July 16-17.
newsitem.headline: U.S.-Cuba migration talks set for July 16-17.

text.p: The United States and Cuba will hold a new round of talks in New York on July 16 and 17 to discuss migration issues, the State Department said on Tuesday.

Spokesman John Dinger said the talks, seventh in a series, would be "to review technical details and ensure the continued smooth operation and implementation of the migration agreements" between the two countries.
No other issues would be addressed, Dinger told a news briefing.
Under agreements signed in 1994 and 1995, the United States turns back illegal "boat people" trying to cross the Straits of Florida from Cuba but accepts up to 20,000 legal immigrants per year.
The United States has maintained an economic embargo on Cuba for 35 years and has no diplomatic relations with the communist-ruled island.
